title: unify-tfstate-backend-and-gpu-nodepool-labeling-for-private-deploys
author: Anita Kaur
commits: feat(tfstate): consolidate backend key schema and add per-environment prefixing
refactor(gpu): add canonical labels and knobs for autoscaler + node selectors
chore(iam): split nodepool role and tighten permissions for instance profiles
description:
Motivation: Private deployments have diverged across customers: some clusters used per-VPC tfstate buckets, others used per-cluster keys, and GPU node pools lacked consistent labels that our autoscaler and cost tooling rely on. This PR unifies the tfstate backend layout, introduces canonical GPU nodepool labels/metadata, and modularizes IAM role surfaces to reduce blast radius and make upgrades/rollbacks safer.

Changes (high level):
- modules/state/backend.tf: new unified backend key pattern (bucket /<org>/<env>/redwood-private.tfstate) with an optional legacy migration flag. Supports both S3 and GCS via provider-agnostic variables.
- scripts/tfstate-migrator/migrate.sh: helper to detect legacy state objects and perform terraform state mv/import under a dry-run flag. Adds consistent locking hints and post-migration verification steps.
- modules/gpu-pool/*: node pool module now injects standardized tags/labels: redwood.org, redwood.env, redwood.pool-type=gpu, redwood.gpu-class; exposes optional node taints and kubelet args for NUMA/mtune. Readme documents compatibility with cluster-autoscaler label selectors.
- modules/iam/*: split into iam/nodepool_role and iam/admin_role abstractions; least-privilege defaults and a documented opt-out for legacy workflows. Added policy attachment moving from monolithic role to smaller role-per-responsibility.
- modules/network/shared_vpc_peering.tf: optional module to configure cross-project VPC peering and route propagation for air-gapped hybrid customers.
- docs/private/state-migration.md: step-by-step runbook and rollback instructions, including sample terraform commands and S3/GCS object snapshots.

Checklist: (x) unit/integration plan checked locally; (x) migration script tested against a staging bucket; (x) reviewers added; (x) docs updated.

Testing / Validation:
- Ran terraform plan/apply against a staging project using the migrator in dry-run mode, validated that state mv commands map resources to the new key layout without resource replacement.
- Deployed a GPU nodepool to a test cluster and verified labels appear on Node objects and that cluster-autoscaler picks them up with selector redwood.pool-type=gpu.
- IAM module unit tests validated with kitchen/inspec (policy lint) and validated that node instance profile permissions are sufficient for kubelet and NVIDIA driver provisioner only.

Upgrade path and migration plan:
1) Run scripts/tfstate-migrator/migrate.sh --dry-run against your existing state to collect candidate keys.
2) Review generated mapping and run migrate.sh (non-dry-run) to copy/move state into the new backend key. The script performs a terraform init -migrate-state under the hood.
3) Run terraform plan against the new backend; expect no resource diffs if migration succeeds.
4) If anything fails, follow rollback: restore bucket snapshot (instructions in docs/private/state-migration.md) and revert the backend config.

Rollback considerations:
- We explicitly do NOT attempt in-place live renames of provider-managed resources. The migrator is conservative: it moves terraform state only, leaving cloud resources untouched. Snapshots are required before running any state migration.
- If a migration partially completes, the runbook includes steps to re-run the migrate script referencing the checkpoint manifest.

Security notes:
- IAM changes reduce iam:PassRole and wide admin bindings; default new roles are narrower. Customers with custom bindings must opt-out and provide a mapping.

Related tickets / context: Linear ENG-1124 (private deployment state drift) and INF-78 (GPU autoscaler label standardization). Support case SUP-4321 reported a migration failure; this PR includes the fix.

Why this approach? Centralizing the backend key namespace avoids dozens of ad-hoc state keys we've accumulated and makes user-facing runbooks simpler. Canonical GPU labels simplify autoscaling, cost attribution, and cross-team policies. Modular IAM reduces blast radius during upgrades.
review_comments: Diego Ramos: +1 on the labeling change — can we make redwood.gpu-class optional with a default of 'nvidia-a100' so older clusters don't break?
Anita Kaur: Good call; made redwood.gpu-class optional with default and added a note to README about explicit overrides.
Priya Menon: Migration script looks good. One request: add a --backup-bucket flag for customers who want state snapshots in a different bucket.
Anita Kaur: Added --backup-bucket and updated docs with examples. Also added a safety check to prevent migration if lock TTL is too low.
Ethan Zhou: IAM policy change is safer; recommend an automated policy diff as part of CI to avoid surprise privilege escalation in enterprise upgrades.
Anita Kaur: Filed follow-up ENG-1149 for a CI policy-diff job; included a note in the release notes.
release_notes: Private deploy: unified tfstate backend key schema; migration helper for legacy states; standardized GPU nodepool labels for autoscaler and cost tooling; modular IAM roles to minimize privileges; optional shared VPC peering module. See docs/private/state-migration.md for migration/runbook.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: state migration is high-risk for customers with manual state edits. Mitigation: dry-run mode, required bucket snapshots, backup-bucket option, and explicit manual approval step in the runbook. Added conservative default IAM policies to avoid accidental privilege increases.
notes_for_release_engineering: Coordinate with SRE to open a 2-hour maintenance window for customer migrations. Provide customers the migrate.sh script and sample mapping output in a secure channel. Ensure terraform state locking is enabled (Dynamo/CloudLock) before migration.
